note: THE RECORD THAT NAMES THE CROSS STREETS. Answering the Council's order of 17 October 1904, the Superintendent of Streets had each ward superintendent report the square yards of each kind of pavement 'in need of repair' on streets whose guaranty had expired. The First Ward's macadam list reads: '18th street, from Indiana avenue to Calumet avenue (macadam) 1,857; 20th street, from Indiana avenue to Calumet avenue (macadam) 1,466; 21st street, from Michigan avenue to Calumet avenue (macadam) 2,713; Prairie avenue, from 20th street to 22d street (macadam) 1,662; Calumet avenue, from 21st street to 403 feet north of 20th street (macadam) 1,857' (p. 1699). A surface out of its guaranty and in need of repair five months after the scene date was there on it, and the Board's list of 2 November 1903 shows none of these was laid by the Board in 1901-03. Prairie Avenue 20th-22nd was repaved with asphalt by the Barber Asphalt Paving Co. before 7 November 1906 (chicago_council_proceedings_1907_v58).
what_it_supplies: that on 1 December 1904 E. 18th Street (Indiana to Calumet), E. 20th Street (Indiana to Calumet), E. 21st Street (Michigan to Calumet), Prairie Avenue (20th to 22nd) and Calumet Avenue (403 ft north of 20th to 21st) were macadam, worn and out of guaranty
what_it_does_not_supply: a street not in need of repair, which the list does not name
